```{r master-opts, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = TRUE, warning = FALSE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())

# Marks this as the master document. Each child workflow checks for this flag
# and skips its own run chunk, so no stage is executed twice.
.in_master <- TRUE

run_start <- Sys.time()
```

# How to use this document

1. Put the ChromaTOF export (for example `YP1.csv`) into **`data_raw/`**.
   It goes there **once** — Workflows 1, 2 and 3 all read the same file.
2. Set the sample name near the top of `Rmarkdown/00_setup.Rmd`:

   ```r
   sample_name <- "YP1"
   ```
3. Knit this document (the **Knit** button in RStudio, or
   `rmarkdown::render("run_all.Rmd")`).

Knitting produces a single HTML report showing what every stage did — how many
peaks entered, how many survived each filter, and what was written where. Any
package that is not already installed is installed automatically by the setup
stage, so the project runs on a clean machine without preparation.

**Outputs**

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `results_final/<sample>_final_PAC_report.csv` | Integrated WF4 report |
| `kmd_final/standards_kmd_HCl.png` | H/Cl models, training data only (no sample) |
| `kmd_final/standards_kmd_Br2.png` | Br₂ models, training data only (no sample) |
| `kmd_final/standards_kmd_CH2.png` | CH₂ models, training data only (no sample) |
| `kmd_final/<sample>_kmd_HCl.png` | H/Cl series KMD plot, this sample |
| `kmd_final/<sample>_kmd_Br2.png` | Br₂ series KMD plot, this sample |
| `kmd_final/<sample>_kmd_CH2.png` | CH₂ series KMD plot, this sample |

Every intermediate file each workflow writes is retained in `results_wf1/` to
`results_wf4/` so the route to any result can be traced.

---

# Structure of the pipeline

Workflows 1, 2 and 3 are **independent**. Each interrogates the same peak list
from a different angle, and none is sufficient alone. Only Workflow 4 depends on
the other three.

| | Question asked | Nature of the evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **WF1** | Does this peak match an authentic standard? | Spectral match + retention time |
| **WF2** | Does this peak contain Cl or Br? | Isotope ratios — a physical constant |
| **WF3** | Does this peak contain a ring N, S or O? | Diagnostic neutral losses, mass defect |
| **WF4** | What do all three together support? | Convergence of independent evidence |

Because the three workflows fail in different ways, agreement between them is
meaningful — which is what makes a reported identification defensible.

Each workflow below is a separate R Markdown document under `Rmarkdown/` and can
be knitted, described and cited on its own. This document simply runs them in
order and collects the output.

---

# Setup and configuration

All tolerances, thresholds and file paths are defined here and nowhere else, so
a parameter cannot drift out of sync between workflows.

```{r load-setup, child = "Rmarkdown/00_setup.Rmd"}
```

# Shared helper functions

Functions used by more than one workflow. Keeping them in one place guarantees
that, for example, WF1 and WF3 reshape spectra identically, and that WF2 and the
KMD stage compute Kendrick mass defects with identical constants.

```{r load-helpers, child = "Rmarkdown/01_helpers.Rmd"}
```

# Reference library validation

This runs **before any sample data is processed**. A wrong tabulated mass causes
a compound to disappear silently rather than raise an error, so every reference
table is checked by recomputing each compound's monoisotopic mass from its own
molecular formula.

```{r load-validate, child = "Rmarkdown/02_validate_libraries.Rmd"}
```

```{r run-validation}
run_library_validation()
```

# Workflow 1 — Library matching

```{r load-wf1, child = "Rmarkdown/10_wf1_library_match.Rmd"}
```

```{r run-wf1}
wf1_out <- run_wf1(sample_name)
```

# Workflow 2 — Halogenated PAC filter

```{r load-wf2, child = "Rmarkdown/20_wf2_halogen_filter.Rmd"}
```

```{r run-wf2}
wf2_out <- run_wf2(sample_name)
```

# Workflow 3 — NSO heterocyclic PAC screen

```{r load-wf3, child = "Rmarkdown/30_wf3_hpac_filter.Rmd"}
```

```{r run-wf3}
wf3_out <- run_wf3(sample_name)
```

# Workflow 4 — Evidence integration

```{r load-wf4, child = "Rmarkdown/40_wf4_integration.Rmd"}
```

```{r run-wf4}
wf4_out <- run_wf4(sample_name)
```

# KMD confidence assessment and final plots

```{r load-kmd, child = "Rmarkdown/50_kmd_confidence.Rmd"}
```

Model fitting is independent of any sample. `build_kmd_models()` fits the 12
regression models and saves `kmd_final/standards_kmd_*.png` — the fitted
lines plotted against the training data only, with no sample overlaid — so
the models can be inspected on their own before being applied to real data.

```{r build-kmd-models}
kmd_models <- build_kmd_models()
```

```{r run-kmd}
kmd_out <- run_kmd(sample_name, models = kmd_models)
```

# High-confidence halo-PAC integration

Combines the two independent-ish halogen evidence streams — WF2 (isotope
pattern + exact-mass match) and KMD (homologous-series regression) — into a
single tiered list. KMD is used for class corroboration and anomaly flagging,
not as independent proof of halo-PAC identity; the child document explains why.

```{r load-hc, child = "Rmarkdown/60_high_confidence_halo_pacs.Rmd"}
```

```{r run-hc}
hc_out <- run_high_confidence_halo_pacs(sample_name)
```

# Final report

```{r final-table}
# The integrated report, highest-reliability peaks first.
if (!is.null(wf4_out)) {
  wf4_out
}
```

```{r final-plots, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", results="asis"}
# Display the standards-only diagnostic plots first (model fit, no sample
# data), then the sample-specific plots, for each series in turn.
cat("\n\n### Model diagnostics — training data only, no sample overlaid\n\n")
for (ser in c("HCl", "Br2", "CH2")) {
  f <- file.path(dir_kmd, sprintf("standards_kmd_%s.png", ser))
  if (file.exists(f)) {
    cat(sprintf("\n\n**%s series (standards only)**\n\n", ser))
    cat(sprintf('<img src="%s" style="width:100%%;">\n\n', f))
  }
}

cat(sprintf("\n\n### %s — tested against the models\n\n", sample_name))
for (ser in c("HCl", "Br2", "CH2")) {
  f <- file.path(dir_kmd, sprintf("%s_kmd_%s.png", sample_name, ser))
  if (file.exists(f)) {
    cat(sprintf("\n\n**%s series**\n\n", ser))
    cat(sprintf('<img src="%s" style="width:100%%;">\n\n', f))
  }
}
```

```{r session-summary, echo=FALSE}
elapsed <- round(as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), run_start, units = "secs")), 1)
message("Run complete in ", elapsed, " s")
tibble::tibble(
  Item = c("Sample", "WF3 scoring scheme", "Run time (s)", "Final report",
           "KMD plots"),
  Value = c(sample_name, wf3_scoring, as.character(elapsed),
            file.path("results_final", paste0(sample_name, "_final_PAC_report.csv")),
            "kmd_final/")
)
```
